zh: flow
資安管理的完整決策循環
教學重繪，非官方流程圖。法律與契約、政策、授權、責任及證據留存約束全程；各活動可交錯，改善會回饋風險評估。
風險管理 Risk Management
確認重要資產與威脅，評估可能性、影響及現有控制，決定優先順序與複查時間。
事件應變 Incident Response
查核告警與原始證據，依授權圍堵、處理原因並驗證復原，不憑猜測結案。
改善治理 Continuous Improvement
找出偵測與流程缺口，更新權限、制度、演練及訓練。
回到風險管理
用事後經驗重新評估殘餘風險。修好漏洞不等於管理完所有風險；關閉告警不等於確認沒事。
cards
風險評估與四種處置方向
示意比較：同樣的共享權限錯誤，在可能性相同時，公開海報與私人文件仍可能有不同影響。不是組織通用的量化公式。
案例 A：公開活動海報
資料原本對外公開。示意為可能性中、影響低；仍須檢查其他存取與完整性問題。
案例 B：客戶私人文件
同樣的設定可能造成隱私、法遵與信任損害。示意為可能性中、影響高。
降低 Mitigate
修正共享權限、增加檢測並重新驗證。
避免 Avoid
取消不必要的公開分享功能，也可能犧牲便利性。
移轉／分擔 Transfer / Share
以契約或保險分配部分損失，不代表法定責任全部消失。
接受 Accept
由有權責的人理解風險後決定，留下理由與複查時間；不得逃避法律義務。
殘餘風險 Residual Risk
修好權限仍須確認先前存取與其他缺口；風險不一定歸零。
flow
從告警到事件應變
大量下載不等於已證實入侵。這是方便閱讀的教學順序；保全、圍堵與調查可能並行或反覆，不能為等齊證據而延誤必要處置。
觀察與告警 Event / Alert
系統記錄大量下載並發出通知：先區分觀察事實與需要查證的推測。
查證 Triage
比對身分與權限、時間與來源、資料內容、業務核准，以及原始日誌的完整性與時間一致性。
依證據判定
合理且已授權：記錄理由；證據不足：保留紀錄並補查；疑似或確認事件：依分級程序啟動應變。
證據保全與圍堵
依程序保存紀錄並限制損害，不是一律先關機或刪檔；兼顧服務與病人安全。
根除與復原
處理已確認原因與受影響元件，驗證服務可靠且可用。
改善與並行義務
檢查流程缺口、更新控制；通知義務、法遵與服務衝擊要並行評估。
cards
CSF 2.0 與法遵地圖
六個功能是同時運作的管理面向，不是六個必須依序跑完的關卡。治理橫跨各項工作，事件應變平時也必須準備。
Govern 治理
策略、責任、政策、風險容忍度與監督。
Identify 識別
盤點資產，辨認並評估風險。
Protect 保護
控制存取與權限，降低事件發生機會與影響。
Detect 偵測
觀察異常，產生可查證的訊號。
Respond 回應
判定事件，協調處置並限制損害。
Recover 復原
恢復重要服務，確認可靠且可用。
法律／法規
依適用條件履行法定義務，例如個資法、針對特定對象的資安法。
標準／產業要求
ISO/IEC 27001 管理系統、PCI DSS 支付卡資料安全；契約或法規可能使其成為義務。
框架 Framework
NIST CSF 2.0 協助盤點能力、目標與缺口。
內部政策／程序
寫清楚授權、責任、事件升級與通報方式。通過驗證不等於不會發生事件。
en: flow
The security-management decision cycle

Educational redraw, not an official process diagram. Law, contracts, policy, authorization, accountability and evidence handling apply throughout. Activities may overlap; improvement feeds risk assessment.
Risk Management
Identify important assets and threats; assess likelihood, impact and existing controls; set priorities and review dates.
Incident Response
Check alerts against original evidence. Contain harm, address causes and verify recovery within authorization; do not close a case on guesses.
Continuous Improvement
Find detection and process gaps; update access, procedures, exercises and training.
Return to risk management
Use lessons learned to reassess residual risk. Fixing one vulnerability does not manage every risk; closing an alert does not prove safety.
cards
Risk assessment and four response directions
Illustrative comparison: with the same sharing error and likelihood, public posters and private files may still have different impacts. This is not a universal numerical formula.
Case A: public event posters
The information was intended for public access: medium likelihood, low impact in this illustration. Still check other access and integrity concerns.
Case B: private customer files
The same error may harm privacy, compliance and trust: medium likelihood, high impact in this illustration.
Mitigate
Correct sharing permissions, add detection and verify again.
Avoid
Cancel an unnecessary public-sharing feature, possibly sacrificing convenience.
Transfer / Share
Allocate some losses through contracts or insurance; legal responsibilities do not simply disappear.
Accept
An authorized accountable owner understands the risk and records reasons and a review date. Acceptance cannot evade law.
Residual Risk
Check earlier access and remaining gaps after fixing permissions. Risk need not become zero.
flow
From an alert to incident response

Bulk downloading does not prove compromise. This is an instructional reading order: preservation, containment and investigation may overlap or repeat. Do not delay necessary action while waiting for perfect evidence.
Event / Alert
A system records bulk downloads and issues a notification. Separate observations from hypotheses.
Triage
Check identity and permissions, time and origin, data content, business approval, and the completeness and time consistency of original logs.
Evidence-based decision
Authorized and reasonable: record why. Insufficient evidence: preserve records and investigate. Suspected or confirmed incident: activate the appropriate response procedure.
Preserve evidence and contain
Preserve records and limit harm under procedure; do not automatically power off or delete files. Consider service and patient safety.
Eradicate and recover
Address confirmed causes and affected components; verify that services are trustworthy and available.
Improve and meet parallel obligations
Fix process gaps and update controls. Assess notification duties, compliance and service impact in parallel.
cards
CSF 2.0 and the compliance map
The six Functions are concurrent management areas, not six gates to finish in order. Govern spans the work; incident response also requires preparation during normal operations.
Govern
Strategy, accountability, policy, risk tolerance and oversight.
Identify
Inventory assets and identify and assess risks.
Protect
Manage access and permissions; reduce incident likelihood and impact.
Detect
Observe anomalies and produce signals that can be investigated.
Respond
Determine incidents, coordinate action and limit harm.
Recover
Restore important services and verify trustworthiness and availability.
Laws and regulations
Fulfil duties when statutory applicability conditions are met, such as privacy law and cybersecurity law for specified entities.
Standards and industry requirements
ISO/IEC 27001 for management systems and PCI DSS for payment-card data. Contracts or law can make requirements binding.
Framework
NIST CSF 2.0 helps identify capabilities, objectives and gaps.
Internal policy and procedures
Specify authorization, responsibility, escalation and reporting. Certification does not guarantee that incidents cannot occur.
